cells.tense: Right now you are the one reading this honestly, with your own eyes on it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you can clear today, tell the person it touches that you're setting it down, and end it in your own words.
cells.core: You can see what's finished here and you say so out loud. The pattern reads clean, the clearing gets done, and neither one needs a speech. People get decisions around you without being managed, because the decision is already visible before you make it. That is rare, and it is also delicate. When you can see what an ending will cost someone, the pull of what they might feel becomes a reason to slow the thing down, and endings don't hold well in slow motion. Reading happens in a moment; so does recognition. You can say what you saw and what it deserves, and let someone meet it from where they actually are. Say the clear thing while it is still clear. That is the whole of it, and it holds what you have.

cells.verb: reading the pattern underneath and acting on what it shows

cells.tense: Your attention is already at the next threshold, deciding what it will be before the current room is even cleared.
cells.ask: Once today, before you decide where something is heading, put in writing what is actually in front of you, and let that page set the next move.
cells.core: You are running the endings ahead of the ending. The pattern is being read before it has fully formed, so everything feels like it is already decided and you are just catching up. That is exhausting, and it costs exactly the thing you do best. When you arrive at a threshold already knowing how it goes, the clearing does not get done, it gets narrated, and the people standing in it can feel the difference. You've stopped looking and started forecasting. The next step is supposed to come from what is actually there, not from what you already expect. Write down what is actually in front of you before you decide where it is heading, and let the writing set the next move. It will cost you the head start. It hands you back the reading.
cells.sheetLine: You're living at the next threshold before you've crossed this one.

cells.tense: Part of you is still standing at a door that closed a while back, waiting for it to open again.
cells.ask: Tell one person the short true version of what happened, keep it to five minutes, and let them hear it without asking anything back.
cells.core: You already have the read on what ended. It just hasn't been handed to anyone, including you, so the clearing cannot happen and things keep their shape past the point where they'd naturally give way. This is not a failure of insight. It is insight held privately longer than it can survive. The pattern keeps arriving and you keep it in the room with you. What might move it is not more thinking. It is one person hearing the short true version, spoken, with nothing asked in return. You do not have to believe the ending is handled to say what happened. Say the short version once, to someone who will just take it. What they do with it is theirs. The saying is yours, and it is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You know what ended. It has only ever been yours to hear.
cells.verb: reading the pattern underneath and acting on what it shows

cells.tense: You are already clearing this room and talking about it like the room is clearing itself.
cells.ask: Name one thing you let end on purpose this month, say out loud that it was your call, and keep that sentence as the record of it.
cells.core: The endings are already happening, and the pattern-finding is already doing the work. You are just describing it as something that befell you — things ran their course, it was time, it fell apart. Some of that is true. Some of it is you, deciding, and not signing it. Naming that matters because a clearing you did not claim is a clearing you cannot trust, and trust is what lets you stand in the next room without bracing for the same disappearance. This is not a critique of your method. It is a smaller, more exact version of what has actually been going on. One ending you let happen on purpose this month, said plainly as yours, with no explanation attached. Say it once, the way you'd say it to someone who already knows. That sentence is yours to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You're already clearing this. You keep saying it happened to you.
